headline: 242 people die daily as air pollution kills 88,000 annually in Bangladesh
summary: A Jahangirnagar University study reveals that PM2.5 pollution costs the economy $23 billion a year, roughly 5% of the country's GDP.
details: A new study by researchers at Jahangirnagar University estimates that fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution kills approximately 242 people every day across six major cities in Bangladesh.
The research indicates that about 88,240 premature deaths occur annually due to PM2.5 pollution in Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Khulna, Sylhet, and Barishal.
Beyond the health toll, the study estimates an annual economic loss of nearly $23 billion (Tk 2.8 trillion), representing about 5% of Bangladesh's gross domestic product (GDP).
Ischemic heart disease was the leading cause of PM2.5-related deaths, claiming 37,519 lives annually, followed by chronic respiratory diseases (8,344) and lung cancer (811).
Dhaka recorded the highest number of premature deaths, with 68,703 annually, followed by Chattogram with 11,202.
The study, led by Associate Professor Dr Md Sakhawat Hossain, found that PM2.5-related deaths increased steadily across all six cities between 2013 and 2021, with the sharpest rise in Dhaka.
Researchers warn that without immediate and effective interventions, the health and economic burdens will continue to grow.
The study recommends adopting evidence-based pollution control policies and strengthening urban air quality management to protect public health.
caption:
242 people die every single day in Bangladesh due to air pollution. That's over 88,000 lives lost every year.

A new study by researchers at Jahangirnagar University estimates that fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution kills approximately 242 people every day across six major cities in Bangladesh.

The research indicates that about 88,240 premature deaths occur annually due to PM2.5 pollution in Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Khulna, Sylhet, and Barishal.

Beyond the health toll, the study estimates an annual economic loss of nearly $23 billion (Tk 2.8 trillion), representing about 5% of Bangladesh's gross domestic product (GDP).

Ischemic heart disease was the leading cause of PM2.5-related deaths, claiming 37,519 lives annually, followed by chronic respiratory diseases (8,344) and lung cancer (811).

Dhaka recorded the highest number of premature deaths, with 68,703 annually, followed by Chattogram with 11,202.

The study, led by Associate Professor Dr Md Sakhawat Hossain, found that PM2.5-related deaths increased steadily across all six cities between 2013 and 2021, with the sharpest rise in Dhaka.

Researchers warn that without immediate and effective interventions, the health and economic burdens will continue to grow.

The study recommends adopting evidence-based pollution control policies and strengthening urban air quality management to protect public health.

headline_marked: Govt [[does not believe in politics of religious division]], says Fakhrul
headline: Govt does not believe in politics of religious division, says Fakhrul
summary: Local Government Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir urges citizens to remain united against efforts to disrupt communal harmony during the Rath Jatra festival.
details: Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stated that Bangladesh is a country for people of all faiths and does not belong to any single religion.

Speaking at the Sri Sri Jagannath Rath Jatra Festival 2026 at Swamibagh Ashram in Dhaka, the minister emphasized that the government is committed to advancing the country by bringing together people of all faiths.
Fakhrul noted that the government does not believe in politics that seeks to divide people on religious grounds, prioritizing instead national development and public welfare.
Recalling the Liberation War of 1971, he highlighted how Hindus, Muslims, Buddhists, and Christians fought together for the country's independence.
The minister alleged that certain 'vested quarters' have repeatedly tried to weaken the tradition of communal harmony and urged citizens to resist such attempts.
The Rath Jatra festival, organized by ISKCON Bangladesh at the Swamibagh Ashram, is an annual Hindu religious celebration that attracts thousands of devotees each year.
